newsitem.title: UK: DKB bets on Brazil, Peru, Venezuela as 1997 winners.
newsitem.headline: DKB bets on Brazil, Peru, Venezuela as 1997 winners.

text.p: Dresdner Kleinwort Benson on Monday tipped Brazil, Peru and Venezuela to be Latin America's top performers for 1997, but predicted disappointment in store from Mexico and Argentina.
After a year in which the region's bond markets surprised investors by outperforming stocks, DKB strategists said equities would recoup lost ground in the year ahead.
"We expect a stronger performance from equities in 1997," DKB said in a note to investors, adding earnings per share (EPS) for the region would rise in the range of 20 to 25 percent.
The wild card remained the Mexican peso -- how fast it devalued towards year-end forecasts of 9.55 pesos to the dollar would help determine those EPS levels, it said.
DKB said it preferred Brazil, Peru and Venezuela of Latin America's seven major markets, offering the best combination of valuations and potential earnings growth in the year ahead.

It saw broader participation in the Brazilian market, with increased bullishness among U.S. investors, and predicted prices as measured by the Morgan Stanley Capital International Index (MSCII) for Brazil rising about 50 percent, fuelled by earnings growth of 32 percent.
DKB predicted Peru's GDP growth accelerating to 4.6 percent in 1997 from 1.7 in 1996, and its market, led by investable stocks in the mining and telecom sector, rising with it.
Forecasting returns of over 25 percent, it cautioned however that this could be dampened by any perceived rise in terrorism.
"Any suggestion of a return to instability and violence would alarm investors," it added.

Venezuela, the best performer on the International Finance Corporation's composite investable index with gains of 117.7 percent over 1996, is forecast to make gains of 32 percent based on profit expansion and a contraction in multiples as earnings growth comes down to sustainable levels, DKB said.
But its outlook for Mexico was bearish.
"The major disappointments will come in Mexico and, to a lesser extent, Argentina," it said.

"We anticipate a disappointing US dollar return (from Mexico) of minus 26 percent," it said, adding the Mexican market should underperform the MSCII LatAm index by roughly 50 percentage points in 1997 due to a decline in the peso and contracting stock multiples.
Argentina's fortunes would depend more on shifting investor sentiment rather than on changing fundamentals, it said, adding now was the time to be underweight.
It said it expected a dollar return for investors of minus four percent. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
